sources.entry: CoreLocationCLI - Get the physical location of your device and prints it to standard output

summary.one_liner: CoreLocationCLI is a macOS command-line tool that prints the device's physical location (latitude and longitude, plus optional reverse-geocoded address details) to standard output.
summary.what_it_does: It reads the Mac's current location through CoreLocation and prints it, by default as "latitude longitude". With --watch it keeps printing updates as the device moves until stopped with CTRL-C. A --format option takes a template with specifiers such as %latitude, %longitude, %altitude, %speed, %h_accuracy, %time, and reverse-geocoded fields like %address, %locality, %country, and %timeZone. A --json option prints all available fields as a single JSON object. A --verbose option shows debugging output.
use_cases: get current location from the terminal
reverse geocode coordinates to an address
test location-dependent software on a Mac
feed location data into other command-line tools
notable: Output is customizable with format specifiers, including reverse-geocoded address fields
Full JSON output of all available location fields
Watch mode prints location updates as the device moves
Distributed as a notarized release installable via Homebrew cask
Release artifacts are signed with GitHub attestations (SLSA provenance)
caveats: Requires macOS; Wi-Fi must be turned on or it reports kCLErrorDomain error 0
On first run an unidentified-developer dialog may appear if the copy is not the notarized release; approve it in System Settings, Privacy & Security
Building from source requires steps described in scripts/README.md, which were not reviewed here
keywords: alternative to location apps on mac
